title: A finite type algebra over a field has finitely many isolated spectrum points
statement: Let $k$ be a field and let $A$ be a finitely generated $k$-algebra [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra]. Then the set of prime ideals $\mathfrak q\subset A$ for which $\{\mathfrak q\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] is finite.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00UK (lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite), proof lines 40362-40420: the finite-type fibre has finitely many isolated points

proof.text: The field k is Noetherian. Apply Algebra.FiniteType.isNoetherianRing k A, the Mathlib declaration of [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian], to obtain IsNoetherianRing A.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00UK (lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite), proof lines 40384-40390: the fibre algebra is finite type over the field and hence Noetherian

proof.text: PrimeSpectrum.finite_setOfPred_isMin A packages finiteness of minimal primes [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-finitely-many-minimal-primes] and injectivity of the map from spectrum points to their prime ideals. Hence the set of minimal spectrum points is finite.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00UK (lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite), proof lines 40384-40390, using Lemma Tag 00FR (lemma-Noetherian-irreducible-components)

proof.text: An open singleton is stable under generalization by IsOpen.stableUnderGeneralization. PrimeSpectrum.stableUnderGeneralization_singleton identifies this condition with membership of the associated ideal in minimalPrimes A, and PrimeSpectrum.isMin_iff identifies it with minimality of the spectrum point. This is the basic-open minimality argument already packaged in Mathlib; no localization result is used.

source.place: Algebra, Lemma Tag 00UK (lemma-etale-makes-quasi-finite-finite), proof lines 40362-40368, where isolated points of the finite-type fibre are counted; the minimality argument uses Lemma Tag 00E0 (lemma-Zariski-topology), part (14)

proof.text: Using Set.Finite.subset, include the set of points with open singleton in the finite set of minimal spectrum points from step 2. The types and topologies of Spec (CommRingCat.of A) and PrimeSpectrum A are definitionally equal.

split_report.summary: Checked Algebra Lemma 00UK (proof lines 40384-40404), which counts isolated closed points of the finite-type fibre for induction. This item proves the stronger finiteness of all isolated points. Finite type over the field makes A Noetherian via 00FN; 00FR gives finitely many minimal primes; an open singleton prime is minimal by the basic-open basis (00E0 (14)); hence the isolated-prime set is a subset of a finite set. No new node was needed, and the item's existing Mathlib searches were retained.
